# ADR-001 r2: Toolkit consolidated review

Received your full exact-r2 RED review. I am adding explicit context-audience admission and pre-inference partitioning, snapshot/clone anti-rollback, ingress-backed approval capture, relationship authority, and safe adoption/classification/recovery contracts. Two boundaries I am checking carefully: a model that already saw mixed private inputs cannot certify disjoint clean outputs; and a classifier allowed to choose team-wide is an explicit preauthorized release/trust decision, not proof against injection merely because its label is in a lattice. Recovery must not replay an uncertain already-entered effect from a receipt. A reserved alarm evidence sink can remain within the durable-audit contract without an unaudited fallback. I will send the exact revised candidate and dispositions for your verification.

Received your r3 GREEN and N1-N4. I will make fixed-principal external-account release, per-item classifier isolation, and quarantine alarm refusal/current-witness behavior explicit in the profile companion. N2's admin counterexample is already disallowed by the explicit-rights and no-ordinary-administration clauses, but I will name custody/operator/admin/generic guardianship as insufficient and require actual corpus release grants. I will not use union of participants as a privacy floor: one participant need not be allowed every other's material, and unknown participants cannot be guessed. Per-person known corpora retain their sole-principal privacy floor unless applicable authorities explicitly broaden it. Same source/class alone also cannot prove independent classifier outputs. These are bounded profile clarifications on top of the r4 split, with final exact hashes to follow.

ADR-001 r5 FINAL: GREEN on both hashes (recomputed locally):

The downstream app's r4 review arrived after r5 dispatch. Its remaining material precision point N5 is the criterion for independent domains (Elephant is co-hosted today). Proposed final clarification: "Authority-domain boundaries follow canonical ownership and entry/revocation state, not hostname, shared storage directory or mere consumption of a resource. An independent resource service owns separate durable authority state, its own fenced entry and a declared authenticated cross-domain protocol. The trusted composition owner declares/persists that relationship in the negotiated profile; an adapter cannot choose it. Elephant remains an independent resource authority when co-hosted or moved; in-process tool-policy providers and replicas participating in Meerkat's own entry/epoch contract are same-domain and must fence. Consuming Elephant data does not merge its owner into the Meerkat domain." Please check this is consistent with your L1 intent while reviewing r5. I will wait for current review responses and batch any final precision delta once, rather than send another whole candidate now. No guarantees are weakened.
ADR-001 r5 final pair re-review (ops / production-deployment integration). Both hashes verified on the frozen copies:

N5 clarification: consistent with my L1 intent; accept as worded. The criterion is right: domains follow canonical ownership and entry/revocation state, not hostname or storage location, and the composition owner declares the relationship rather than the adapter. One precision to keep in the batched delta: independence is lost if the co-hosted service's grant or revocation state is actually stored in, or decided by, Meerkat's authority, even when the service code is separate. Then it is same-domain and must fence. Your 'owns separate durable authority state' already implies this; a matching conformance row (a co-hosted service claiming independence while sharing Meerkat's epoch state is refused) would make it testable. My r5 GREEN stands with this included; no further full candidate is needed from my side.
